newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog picks "green" energy projects.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog picks "green" energy projects.

text.p: Electricity regulator Stephen Littlechild on Friday said he selected 95 projects which could supply extra electricity coming from alternative sources such as landfill gas and windmill energy in England and Wales.
The projects could generate the extra 400 to 500 megawatt (MW) of "green" power, which the government has indicated the electricity suppliers might have to buy.

The government has yet to decide exactly how much they will have to purchase. The regional electricity companies are already required to buy 1,251 MW coming from alternative sources. Some 60,000 MW is coming from regular power generators using gas or coal to fire their stations.
Out of a group of 426 bids, Littlechild selected the projects which quoted the lowest prices for their electricity.
Littlechild also formed a "safe" group which in theory could supply a maximum of 750 MW, but would always be good for about 450 MW if some projects would fail.
Liitlechild also picked out 18 groups which could supply 75 MW of "alternative" electricity for Scotland.
Most of the selected projects plan to produce electricity from landfill gas or municipal and industrial waste.
The base case group for England and Wales includes only two wind projects and none based on hydro, energy crops or agricultural waste.
